ai-at-work.title: Source: Elastic agrees to buy CRV-backed DeductiveAI for up to $85M
ai-at-work.excerpt: DeductiveAI, a startup that uses AI to catch and resolve bugs in software, was founded just three years ago.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Elastic, the search and analytics company, is acquiring DeductiveAI, a three-year-old AI startup focused on automated bug detection and resolution, for up to $85 million. This matters to digital workplace professionals because it signals that enterprise software vendors are betting heavily on AI-driven development tools that could reshape how teams build and maintain the applications your business runs on. The real question isn't whether AI will find bugs faster, it's whether it'll find them faster than your team can introduce new ones, and whether Elastic will actually integrate this into their core platform or let it become expensive shelf-ware.

ai-at-work.title: Fabrix.ai demonstrates production-grade agentic operations at Cisco Live
ai-at-work.excerpt: Artificial intelligence dominated headlines and keynotes at every event I’ve attended this year, including the recent Cisco Live 2026. Though the thirst for AI has been insatiable for a couple of year
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Fabrix.ai showed off AI agents actually running in production environments at Cisco Live, moving past the theoretical stage that's dominated AI conversations for two years. Digital workplace pros need to pay attention because autonomous agents handling real operational tasks are coming whether your organization is ready or not, and they'll reshape how we think about IT support and workflow automation. After spending years listening to vendors explain what AI could do someday, it's refreshing to see something that actually works, though I'm guessing half the audience still left thinking "nice demo, call us in five years."

ai-at-work.title: Agentic marketing AI startup Gradial grabs $65M in fresh funding
ai-at-work.excerpt: Seattle-based startup Gradial today revealed it has raised $65 million in a new round of funding to accelerate the development of its agentic artificial intelligence operating system for marketing. To
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Gradial, a Seattle AI startup, just raised $65 million to build an autonomous AI system that handles marketing work without constant human direction. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because agentic AI is coming for marketing operations, and you need to start thinking about how your teams adapt when AI actually does the work instead of just assisting. The real question isn't whether this technology works, it's whether your organization is ready to manage teams where AI colleagues make independent decisions about your brand.

ai-at-work.title: President Trump claims Apple has agreed to buy chips from Intel, boosting its stock
ai-at-work.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump said today that Apple Inc. is going to “design and build” computer chips with Intel Corp. The deal, if confirmed, would be a significant win for Intel, which has struggled
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Trump announced that Apple will design and build chips with Intel, a potential major customer win for the struggling chipmaker. This matters to digital workplace folks because chip supply chains directly impact hardware refresh cycles, device performance, and IT procurement timelines for years to come. If this deal is real, great for Intel's stock price and workers. If it's not, we've just watched another round of "trust me bro" economics play out on social media instead of in actual business press releases.

tools-tech.title: Apple scrambles to handle component price hikes
tools-tech.excerpt: Apple execs are now acknowledging the company is going to need to raises prices to cope with higher component costs, particularly memory. Apple has been battling to avoid doing so, but warned this wee
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple is finally admitting it can't absorb rising component costs anymore and will have to pass price increases along to customers, with industry analysts predicting a roughly 20% bump in smartphone prices across the board. This matters to your workplace because every device refresh cycle just got more expensive, and you'll need to justify those new laptop and phone budgets to finance teams who are already watching pennies. After years of pretending infinite supply chains exist, even Apple can't magic away physics and inflation, which means IT leaders should start having uncomfortable conversations with management about device lifecycle costs right now.

tools-tech.title: France’s OVHcloud bets on frontier AI as Europe seeks alternatives to US models
tools-tech.excerpt: France’s OVHcloud is moving beyond cloud infrastructure into frontier AI model development, a shift that could test whether Europe can produce another serious alternative to US and Chinese AI systems.
tools-tech.dwp_take: OVHcloud is pivoting from pure cloud infrastructure into building its own large language models, aiming to create a European alternative to US and Chinese AI systems. This matters because digital workplace professionals will soon face real choices about where their AI tools come from, which affects everything from data sovereignty to compliance requirements. Honestly, watching Europe try to compete in AI is like watching someone build a Ferrari in a garage while Detroit already has the factory running, but at least they're finally swinging the hammer instead of just complaining about the tools.

tools-tech.title: Android versions: A living history from 1.0 to 17
tools-tech.excerpt: What a long, strange trip it’s been. From its inaugural release to today, Android has transformed visually, conceptually and functionally — time and time again. Google’s mobile operating system may ha
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google's Android OS has evolved dramatically across 17 major versions since its 2008 launch, transforming from a scrappy startup into a refined platform with significant visual, functional, and conceptual changes. Digital workplace pros need to understand Android's trajectory because device management, security protocols, and app compatibility all hinge on knowing which versions are actually in use across your organization. After three decades in this space, I can tell you that every Android update brings a fresh round of "why did IT suddenly break this?" calls, which is basically job security for anyone managing mobile workforces.

tools-tech.title: Adobe: New Firefly Graph can turn creative workflows into reusable assets
tools-tech.excerpt: Adobe’s Firefly Graph is now available to Creative Cloud customers, offering a node-based workflow tool designed to help business create content at scale with generative AI (genAI). With Firefly Graph
tools-tech.dwp_take: Adobe released Firefly Graph, a node-based workflow tool that lets Creative Cloud users chain together AI-powered tasks to automate content creation at scale. This matters because digital workplace teams are drowning in content demands, and anything that lets creatives work smarter instead of harder is worth paying attention to. The real question is whether this actually saves time or just creates another layer of tool complexity that only Adobe's most hardcore users will bother learning.

digital-culture.title: AI took over my life for a year. Here’s what happened
digital-culture.excerpt: Below, Joanna Stern shares five key insights from her new book, I Am Not a Robot: My Year Using AI to Do (Almost) Everything. Joanna is an Emmy-winning tech journalist. She is the founder of New Thing
digital-culture.dwp_take: A tech journalist spent a year letting AI handle most of her work and documented what actually happened in a new book. This matters because it's a real-world stress test of the "AI will do everything" narrative that's flooding boardrooms and your next all-hands meeting. Here's the thing: if someone whose entire job is understanding technology needed a whole year and a book to figure out what AI is actually good for, maybe the rest of us can stop pretending we have it all figured out by next quarter.

digital-culture.title: I drained my 401(k) for an emergency. Here’s what I learned
digital-culture.excerpt: Going from unemployed to full-time consultant was a welcome reprieve. And learning I had time to receive unemployment while trying to figure it out was exactly what I needed. I was very aggressive wit
digital-culture.dwp_take: Someone raided their 401(k) during unemployment and discovered that freelancing at premium rates plus unemployment benefits actually worked out. This matters because digital workplace folks are increasingly consultant-adjacent, juggling gigs and W2 work, so understanding the real financial mechanics of career transitions beats guessing. The real lesson here isn't "drain your retirement accounts"—it's that being choosy about your next gig beats desperation pricing, which honestly most of us learn the hard way.

digital-culture.title: The White House Is Making Up Its Rules for AI in Real Time
digital-culture.excerpt: Anthropic still can’t distribute Claude Mythos or Fable 5 after running afoul of the Trump administration. But no one can say exactly what the company did wrong.
digital-culture.dwp_take: The White House is blocking Anthropic from releasing new AI models without clearly explaining what violated their policies, leaving the company in regulatory limbo. This matters to digital workplace pros because vague AI governance creates uncertainty around which tools you can actually use or recommend to your teams. After three decades in this space, I can tell you that rules written backwards from enforcement actions are how you end up with chaos, not compliance, so someone at the White House needs to write this down before the rest of us are just guessing.

digital-culture.title: Meta’s AI Workers Are Revolting, Peter Thiel’s Secret Society, and SBF’s Plea to Trump
digital-culture.excerpt: On today’s Uncanny Valley, we dive into the dysfunction in Meta’s newly formed AI unit and why it’s been driving already-low employee morale even further into the ground.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Meta's AI unit is hemorrhaging talent because leadership created yet another siloed team with unclear authority and no real integration into existing workflows. This matters because every organization copying Meta's "throw bodies at the problem" approach to AI is about to learn the same expensive lesson: you can't bolt innovation onto a broken culture. The real story here isn't that Meta's best people are leaving. It's that they're leaving because nobody at the top figured out that AI adoption requires actual change management, not just a new org chart and some stock options.

industry-news.title: Alibaba Cloud Bets on France as Europe Seeks More Control Over AI
industry-news.excerpt: Alibaba Cloud opened two Paris availability zones as European enterprises weigh data sovereignty, resilience, and AI infrastructure needs. The post Alibaba Cloud Bets on France as Europe Seeks More Co
industry-news.dwp_take: Alibaba Cloud just opened two data centers in Paris to serve European customers who want their AI infrastructure and data staying put in Europe rather than shipped off to the US or China. This matters because digital workplace leaders are finally waking up to the fact that where your data lives is a business and compliance issue, not just an IT checkbox. Europe's basically saying "we'll take the Chinese cloud provider over the American one if it means keeping our stuff closer to home," which tells you everything you need to know about how much trust has eroded in big tech's data handling.

industry-news.title: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin Targets 2026 Rocket Launch After Cape Canaveral Explosion
industry-news.excerpt: Blue Origin aims to fly New Glenn again in 2026 after a launchpad explosion, amid competition from NASA, Amazon, and SpaceX, raising the stakes. The post Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin Targets 2026 Rocket La
industry-news.dwp_take: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on the launchpad at Cape Canaveral, and the company is now targeting a 2026 retry after investigating what went wrong. This matters to digital workplace folks because space infrastructure failures ripple through cloud services, satellite communications, and the tech supply chains that keep our digital operations humming. Look, if a billionaire can blow up a rocket and just schedule a do-over two years out, maybe your failed Teams migration doesn't feel so catastrophic after all.

industry-news.title: Anthropic Adds Brand Controls, Code Sync to Claude Design
industry-news.excerpt: Anthropic updated Claude Design with design system imports, Claude Code syncing, canvas editing, and more export options for enterprise teams. The post Anthropic Adds Brand Controls, Code Sync to Clau
industry-news.dwp_take: Anthropic rolled out new enterprise features for Claude Design including brand controls, code synchronization, canvas editing, and expanded export options so teams can keep their design systems and code in sync. This matters because design and development teams have spent years drowning in version control nightmares, and anything that reduces the "wait, which file is the source of truth" conversations is worth paying attention to. If Claude can actually help teams stop playing design system whack-a-mole, it might be the first time an AI tool solves a real workplace problem instead of creating five new ones.

industry-news.title: G7 Critical Minerals Push Targets AI and Chip Supply Chain Risk
industry-news.excerpt: The G7’s critical minerals push is putting AI hardware, chip supply chains, data centers, and APAC manufacturing under sharper scrutiny as governments look for ways to finance alternatives to China-li
industry-news.dwp_take: The G7 is pushing governments to finance alternative supply chains for critical minerals used in AI hardware and chips, moving away from China-dependent sources. This matters to digital workplace pros because your organization's ability to deploy new tech, maintain data centers, and scale infrastructure now hinges on geopolitical supply chain decisions you can't control. Here's the kicker: your CIO might finally have a geopolitical excuse for why that new AI initiative got delayed, which beats admitting it was poorly planned.
